paragraphs: comparePackageVersions trims both strings and uses semver.valid/compare only when both are valid; otherwise it returns undefined. isNewerPackageVersion uses positive semantic comparison when available, but falls back to inequality of trimmed strings when either version is invalid. getLatestIceRelease first returns undefined for any truthy getIceEnv('ICE_OFFLINE') value, including strings '0' or 'false'; this is broader than the CLI's true/1/yes parser. Its default URL is https://registry.npmjs.org/<encodeURIComponent(PACKAGE_NAME)>/latest. process.env.ICE_UPDATE_URL overrides only when truthy. new URL errors propagate. HTTPS is required except HTTP is allowed for hostname exactly localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]; username/password are rejected, and redirect:'error' prevents redirects. Fetch uses accept:application/json, AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs??10000), and getIceUserAgent(currentVersion) (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/version-check.ts:7-53).

Non-OK HTTP returns undefined. Parsed metadata must be a non-null non-array object with a trimmed valid semantic-version string. packageName??name may be omitted, otherwise must be a string whose trimmed nonempty value matches the scoped/unscoped package grammar; blank means absent. The default endpoint rejects a different package identity, while an explicitly configured endpoint can hand off to another valid package. note is included only as a trimmed nonempty string. Fetch/JSON/URL errors are not caught in getLatestIceRelease; getLatestIceVersion projects version. checkForNewIceVersion separately skips any truthy ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK, catches all lookup/comparison failures and returns only a newer release. Direct lookup ignores ICE_SKIP_VERSION_CHECK. No disk cache, retry, redirect fallback or network attempt is intrinsic to the helper (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/version-check.ts:54-84).

Rust startup lookup uses crates.io ice-cli metadata, request timeout 1800 ms and user agent ice/<VERSION>. It distinguishes missing(404/410) from transient HTTP/JSON failures and reads crate.max_version. Its semantic comparison strips leading 'v' characters after trim, uses cmp_precedence, and returns false if either parse fails. paragraphs: normalizePath applies resolve then toNamespacedPath. getQuarantineRoot walks upward from the package directory until basename lowercased equals node_modules, returning <node_modules>/.ice-native-quarantine; reaching the filesystem root returns undefined. getLoadedSharedObjects reads process.report.getReport().sharedObjects, returns [] unless an array, ignores nonstrings, normalizes each path and its package root, compares them lowercased, keeps only getCwdRelativePath-contained files, and deduplicates case-insensitively while returning the normalized original spelling (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/windows-self-update.ts:1-46).
records.full_text:
Loaded native files are quarantined under the nearest node_modules directory before a TS package self-update. Later startup attempts best-effort removal of that quarantine, while individual moves preserve a copy at the original package location.

cleanupWindowsSelfUpdateQuarantine returns if no root and recursively force-removes the complete quarantine root, swallowing removal errors. quarantineWindowsNativeDependencies returns if no root or no loaded files; otherwise it creates a unique <Date.now>-<pid>-<randomUUID> run directory. In report order, still-existing loaded files are moved to the same package-relative destination under that run after recursive parent creation, then copied back to the original location. Rename/copy failure propagates; there is no per-file rollback or finally. A failure after rename can therefore leave a moved file without its replacement. This is the source's mutation ordering, not an executed Windows failure (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/windows-self-update.ts:48-84).

The helper itself has no platform guard. Main invokes cleanup only on win32; explicit self-update invocation is CLI-038. No direct helper test was found by the bounded test import/function-name search, so no Windows runtime behavior is claimed.

paragraphs: ensureTool(tool, silent=false) recognizes ICE_OFFLINE values 1/true/yes case-insensitively without trimming. Missing tools in that mode produce optional warnings and undefined. Android produces package-manager guidance and undefined. Otherwise it optionally logs, attempts download, returns the installed path, and catches failures into warning/undefined. No user confirmation is implemented by this helper. Release metadata uses the GitHub latest-release API, User-Agent '<APP_NAME>-coding-agent', a 10-second timeout and unvalidated tag_name with the first 'v' removed. Platform archive templates support Darwin, Linux and Windows with arm64 or otherwise x64; unsupported platforms fail only after metadata lookup. fd on Darwin x64 is pinned to 10.3.0 after the latest-version request. Archive download has a 120-second fetch timeout but no checksum, signature or explicit byte limit (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:112-177; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:333-377).
records.full_text:
The helper prefers a previously installed local executable and then a discovered system command. When neither exists, online non-Android TypeScript sessions may download a platform release and install it in the application bin directory.

TOOLS_DIR is captured from getBinDir at module initialization. Definitions are fd from sharkdp/fd with system names fd then fdfind, and rg from BurntSushi/ripgrep with system name rg. getToolPath first accepts an existing local binary path without checking file kind or executability. It next uses a positive per-tool system-name cache; probes run '<name> --version' synchronously with piped output and no timeout, and accept any result without a spawn error, even a nonzero status. Failed probes are not cached. Existing local/system results are returned before checking offline or platform restrictions (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:1-110).

ensureTool(tool, silent=false) recognizes ICE_OFFLINE values 1/true/yes case-insensitively without trimming. Missing tools in that mode produce optional warnings and undefined. Android produces package-manager guidance and undefined. Otherwise it optionally logs, attempts download, returns the installed path, and catches failures into warning/undefined. No user confirmation is implemented by this helper. Release metadata uses the GitHub latest-release API, User-Agent '<APP_NAME>-coding-agent', a 10-second timeout and unvalidated tag_name with the first 'v' removed. Platform archive templates support Darwin, Linux and Windows with arm64 or otherwise x64; unsupported platforms fail only after metadata lookup. fd on Darwin x64 is pinned to 10.3.0 after the latest-version request. Archive download has a 120-second fetch timeout but no checksum, signature or explicit byte limit (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:112-177; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:333-377).

Downloads use a shared archive filename in TOOLS_DIR and a unique extraction directory. tar handles tar.gz; Windows zip extraction prefers the system tar executable and falls back to PowerShell Expand-Archive with escaped literal paths; other zip platforms try unzip then tar. Extraction subprocesses have no deadline. The executable lookup first accepts expected archive-subdirectory and root paths when they merely exist, then traverses subdirectories to find a regular file with the expected name. It renames into the final bin path, applies 0755 on Unix, and removes archive/extraction paths in finally. A download or temporary-directory failure before the try/finally can leave an archive, and concurrent same-tool downloads share archive/destination paths without single-flight protection. The source performs no archive-containment check of its own. These limitations are not requirements to weaken the native installer (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/utils/tools-manager.ts:178-330).

The only direct test-directory import match was a UI test mocking ensureTool; no dedicated downloader behavior suite was found by the recorded function/import search. Existing tools tests cover the search consumers, not real release downloads. Nothing was executed or downloaded in this audit.

paragraphs: Native changelog.rs already parses entries, embeds bundled release notes, sorts bundled entries, selects the latest release at/below the running version, distinguishes dedicated Ice baseline from compatible legacy baseline, and suppresses first-run notices for a fresh profile. It also supports optional network retrieval with allow_network, ICE_CHANGELOG_URL, a 15-second timeout and fallback to an empty list on load failure (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/changelog.rs:13-34; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/changelog.rs:96-253). Native headings are broader: it trims and accepts leading '#' levels, optional v and missing/invalid minor/patch values defaulting to zero; the heading is excluded from content, and an invalid heading stays in the preceding body. These differ from TS section boundaries. No release-pinned Markdown link normalization is present. Existing inline tests cover native baseline/entry behavior but not the TS link transformation (rust:crates/ice-cli/src/changelog.rs:35-94; rust:crates/ice-cli/src/changelog.rs:255-434).

paragraphs: Download reconstructs an optional header using {type:'header',...header}, followed by all entries, joins with LF without a terminal LF, creates an application/x-ndjson Blob, downloads as header.id or session plus .jsonl, then revokes the object URL. Because the spread follows type, an existing header.type wins. Deep links include leafId and targetId; an injected ice-share-base-url is concatenated with '&'+params, otherwise the current URL keeps its hash and first empty-valued query key as the gist ID. The template does not read ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL or upload a gist; that is a separate TUI share-command boundary. Browser copy tries navigator.clipboard.writeText then hidden-textarea execCommand('copy'), gives a 1500 ms success indicator, and can leave the textarea if the fallback throws before removal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1069-1171).
records.full_text:
The viewer reconstructs a navigable tree from the embedded entries and shows one root-to-leaf conversation path. Its browser controls operate entirely on that data, with optional metadata supplied by a containing share viewer.

Startup decodes base64 through atob→Uint8Array→TextDecoder→JSON.parse with no local catch/schema check. ice-url-params meta content takes precedence over location.search; a truthy leafId parameter wins over the embedded leaf, and targetId controls highlighting/scrolling. Entry and tool-call maps keep the last value for duplicate IDs. Label entries update labels only when both targetId and label are truthy, so a later empty label does not remove an earlier label. Null/undefined/self-parent and orphan entries become roots; children sort by numeric timestamps, roots retain source order. Parent traversal stops for missing/falsy/self parent but has no visited-ID guard, so a multi-node cycle can hang traversal. A robust native export boundary should reject or handle malformed trees instead of copying that weakness (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:8-145).

Clicking a node chooses a descendant by repeatedly following the last timestamp-sorted child; this is a local newest-child walk, not a global maximum timestamp over all leaves. Flattening prefers the active branch and recomputes indentation/connectors after filtering by attaching descendants to the nearest visible ancestor. Filters are default, no-tools, user-only, labeled-only and all. The current leaf is returned before every hide/filter/search check. Other assistant entries without nonblank text are hidden unless stopReason is truthy and neither stop nor toolUse; thus the condition also treats length as exceptional. Default excludes label/custom/model_change/thinking_level_change, no-tools also excludes toolResult, user-only requires a user message, and labeled-only requires a defined label. Search checks that every token appears in lowercased searchable text assembled from labels/roles/content and selected metadata; compaction contributes its type keyword, not the summary body. The search-token initializer at line 369 is connector-redacted, so its exact preprocessing is explicitly unverified (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:155-363; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:374-558).

Initial tree rendering constructs DOM rows/listeners; later navigation updates active classes/path markers without rebuilding the complete filtered order. Search/filter controls force a rebuild. Per-entry content DOM is cached, then cloned on navigation, so expanded/collapsed state is not persistent across branch replacement. Navigation recomputes the global header and selected path, routes a tool-result target to its call element, highlights for 2000 ms and scrolls after a zero-delay timeout. Global stats still describe all embedded entries, not just that selected branch. Invalid truthy leaf IDs can yield an empty path rather than falling back to a valid leaf (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:708-799; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1461-1551; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1853-1865).

Because the spread follows type, an existing header.type wins. Deep links include leafId and targetId; an injected ice-share-base-url is concatenated with '&'+params, otherwise the current URL keeps its hash and first empty-valued query key as the gist ID. The template does not read ICE_SHARE_VIEWER_URL or upload a gist; that is a separate TUI share-command boundary. Browser copy tries navigator.clipboard.writeText then hidden-textarea execCommand('copy'), gives a 1500 ms success indicator, and can leave the textarea if the fallback throws before removal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1069-1171).

Sidebar width persists under localStorage key ice-share:v1:sidebar-width. It starts from CSS defaults400/min240/max840 (JS fallback max720), reserves320px content space, clamps on resize, supports pointer drag and double-click reset, and uses a 900 px mobile query with an overlay toggle. T toggles currently rendered thinking and O tool outputs, except in editable/button targets. Escape clears search and navigates to the original leaf before the editable-element guard; it does not force a full tree rebuild in that path. Toggle booleans are not reapplied automatically to newly cloned branch content. The HTML contains image-modal markup, but this source has no corresponding image-modal activation handler; do not claim implemented image zoom (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/core/export-html/template.js:1644-1865).

paragraphs: Outside ctx.mode==='tui' the command warns and returns. It obtains generic provider auth, warns to use /login llama.cpp if absent, and constructs the router client from result.env.LLAMA_BASE_URL or auth.baseUrl. The first catalog read and every post-action read run through syncCatalog. On read failure, a Retry/Close selector loops only the read; it does not replay a failed mutation. Connection errors are Error instances whose lowercased name/message contain 'fetch failed','timeout' or 'network'. Nonconnection action errors are shown only after a successful reread, while connection-classified action errors are suppressed there. There is no additional ICE_OFFLINE check in this command flow (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:7-40; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:181-227).
records.full_text:
The /llama command opens a dedicated TUI workflow and ignores its command arguments. It coordinates router operations and user decisions; it is not a parser for load/unload/download/login subcommands.

Outside ctx.mode==='tui' the command warns and returns. It obtains generic provider auth, warns to use /login llama.cpp if absent, and constructs the router client from result.env.LLAMA_BASE_URL or auth.baseUrl. The first catalog read and every post-action read run through syncCatalog. On read failure, a Retry/Close selector loops only the read; it does not replay a failed mutation. Connection errors are Error instances whose lowercased name/message contain 'fetch failed','timeout' or 'network'. Nonconnection action errors are shown only after a successful reread, while connection-classified action errors are suppressed there. There is no additional ICE_OFFLINE check in this command flow (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:7-40; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:181-227).

The model list sorts exactly loaded first then ID locale order, displays at most 12 rows and appends the internal '\0download' action. Sleeping models are described and acted on as loaded, but do not receive the list's loaded-sort preference. Context labels use n_ctx??n_ctx_train when truthy, otherwise the first positive finite argument after --ctx-size/-c/-ctx. Confirmed unload awaits unloadAndWait then catalog sync. Loading while other loaded/sleeping models exist asks Unload all and load/Keep loaded and load/Cancel. Replace mode sequentially unloads old models before entering the target-load try block; a failure during that pre-try unload loop can leave earlier models unloaded without restoration. Within the later try/catch, cancelled or failed target load best-effort restores old models sequentially and refreshes; restoration failure preserves the original load error in catch. Cancel sends unload(target), not unloadAndWait (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:64-133; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:23-51; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:321-388).

Download finds a client HF token, opens search, parses a colon only after the first slash, fetches details and shows auto/manual gated-access guidance with Continue/Back. It explicitly tells the user the llama server needs its own authorized HF_TOKEN; the client token is not sent as a router credential. When no quantization was supplied, available options include sizes and Q4_K_M 'recommended'; an already supplied quantization is not checked against the discovered list. It asks the router to download repository[:quant], supports unload-as-cancel, then syncs the returned catalog. Detail fetch itself is not tied to a view-level cancellation signal (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/index.ts:135-179).

Search trims input, requires 2 characters for a new query, debounces500 ms and aborts the previous request. A per-view map caches by lowercase query without TTL/size bound. Responses enter the cache before checking closed/aborted/current-query state, so a stale response can populate cache while leaving the visible state untouched. Fuzzy filtering uses TUI-235 for membership but preserves original API order. Selection clamps after filtering and wraps on up/down; at most 10 centered rows show. Confirm prefers a query matching the exact owner/repository[:quant] regex over the highlighted result, and cancel closes once while clearing debounce/aborting request (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:96-274).

runWithProgress starts the operation immediately and converts success/failure into a fulfilled settlement object. It races that against the progress cancel key, then asks confirmation. A declined confirmation or already completed operation resumes/finishes normally. On confirmed stop it awaits the cancel callback first and aborts the operation controller in finally, then awaits settled and returns cancelled. If cancel itself rejects, control skips the later await/return and propagates that error; the operation's wrapped settlement remains observed. The 40-character bar clamps filled length but prints the raw rounded percentage, with no finite-number guard. showLlamaUi routes run completion to done and errors to notify then done; view content replacement clears the old progress resolver without settling an abandoned progress promise (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:305-319; ice:packages/coding-agent/src/extensions/llama/ui.ts:419-543).

The doc's router setup flags, filesystem examples and server token guidance were read as documentation only. Existing llama tests exercise provider/client fixtures, not this complete UI recovery/cancellation flow. No model server, download, token file or test was invoked.

paragraphs: session_shutdown awaits client.close, whose cancellation semantics are MISC-037. This is an optional extension factory rather than an unconditional startup builtin: the source search finds no main/ICE-launcher import of this factory, and the live fixture explicitly passes its file through --extension after --no-extensions. The fixture describes CLI → local OmniRoute bridge → official Claude SDK → ICE read tool, but it was not executed. Its use of ICE_OFFLINE=1 is not a transport gate: the adapter itself still calls the configured local endpoint. No external bridge source, login session or account was inspected.
records.full_text:
Loading the extension reads its configuration and creates one client shared by that extension instance. It publishes the configured models and a status command; it does not replace the agent loop or install the external bridge.

claudeSdkExtension loads <agentDir>/claude-sdk.json before registering anything, then calls registerProvider('claude-sdk') with name 'Claude Agent SDK (local; billing external)', api 'claude-sdk', the configured baseUrl, a fixed nonsecret API-key marker and streamSimple forwarding directly to client.stream. Each configured model keeps its exact id, gains a '(SDK; billing external)' label, reasoning=true, input ['text','image'], contextWindow=200000, maxTokens=16384 and zero input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite costs. Those costs and catalog limits are metadata, not a billing guarantee or proof of the bridge's actual model capabilities. The adapter enforces its own output ceiling separately (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/extension.ts:7-26).

The extension registers /claude-sdk-status with a handler that ignores command arguments, awaits client.status and sends an info notification. status performs GET <baseUrl>/api/services/claude-sdk/status with a freshly read Bearer token, redirect:error and AbortSignal.timeout(12000). Non-OK responses produce a fixed unavailable/unauthorized message. Successful JSON must be an object containing object authentication; state is restricted to subscription/api_auth/not_logged_in/unknown, otherwise displayed as unknown, and ready is true only for the literal boolean true. Errors produce a fixed reachability message. The JSON body is not size-bounded by this status method, and the custom inference fetch option does not replace this global fetch call (ice:packages/coding-agent/src/claude-sdk/adapter.ts:206-225).

session_shutdown awaits client.close, whose cancellation semantics are MISC-037. This is an optional extension factory rather than an unconditional startup builtin: the source search finds no main/ICE-launcher import of this factory, and the live fixture explicitly passes its file through --extension after --no-extensions. The fixture describes CLI → local OmniRoute bridge → official Claude SDK → ICE read tool, but it was not executed. Its use of ICE_OFFLINE=1 is not a transport gate: the adapter itself still calls the configured local endpoint. No external bridge source, login session or account was inspected.

paragraphs: The root npm eval script forwards to the private @zykairotis/ice-evals workspace. run-evals.mjs accepts --provider value, --model value and their = forms; repeated values overwrite earlier values. Separate-form values must be nonempty and must not start with '-'. After trimming, the presence of either CLI selector requires both CLI values; a missing CLI half is not filled from the environment. Without any CLI selector, trimmed ICE_PROVIDER and ICE_MODEL must either both exist or both be absent. All other arguments are retained in encounter order. There is no special end-of-options escape in this parser, so recognized selectors after a literal '--' are still consumed (ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:16-63).

ICE_EVAL_ARTIFACT_DIR is resolved relative to the package root when truthy; otherwise the runner creates .eval/<ISO timestamp with colons replaced>_<UUID>. The runner gives explicit CLI provider/model values precedence over environment defaults and forwards other arguments to Vitest. A harness may override that default with its own model. The runner and harness validate selection at different points, so launching without a default is allowed only when the executed harnesses supply their own models.

The root npm eval script forwards to the private @zykairotis/ice-evals workspace. run-evals.mjs accepts --provider value, --model value and their = forms; repeated values overwrite earlier values. Separate-form values must be nonempty and must not start with '-'. After trimming, the presence of either CLI selector requires both CLI values; a missing CLI half is not filled from the environment. Without any CLI selector, trimmed ICE_PROVIDER and ICE_MODEL must either both exist or both be absent. All other arguments are retained in encounter order. There is no special end-of-options escape in this parser, so recognized selectors after a literal '--' are still consumed (ice:packages/evals/scripts/run-evals.mjs:16-63).

Both model defaults are installed together or both removed. Spawn errors are thrown; a null child status becomes exit 1, otherwise the child status is propagated. resolveModelSelection uses explicitModel.provider/id via nullish fallback to environment fields, then trims and requires both. An explicit empty string therefore rejects rather than falling back. The local test suite covers explicit precedence, trimming and incomplete selections; it does not execute the runner or a model. Eval configuration runs src/**/*.eval.ts in Node with fileParallelism=false, testTimeout120000, hookTimeout30000, the eval afterEach setup, the external vitest-evals reporter and the local reporter. The separate unit-test configuration selects test/**/*.test.ts. Both use the monorepo source aliases, with an explicit coding-agent index alias; package metadata pins vitest-evals0.15.0 and Vitest4.1.9. Compiler configuration is noEmit/NodeNext through the shared strict ES2022 base. These are source configuration facts, not an assertion that dependencies were installed or tests ran.

recordEvalSourceArtifact records type '@zykairotis/ice-evals:source', a supplied runId and one SourceAttachment. Its TypeScript interface specifies name, contentType, string body and UTF-8 encoding, but this wrapper adds no runtime validation. Unique module-local symbols extend Vitest's TestArtifactRegistry for the two record types; the wire discriminator remains the string type.

persistEvalArtifactReferences walks artifacts in order and selects only these two types whose runId strictly equals the report run ID. It chooses sessions or sources by type. For each attachment it computes basename(name), rejects when that differs from the original name, creates <artifactDirectory>/<category>/<SHA-256(runId)> recursively with requested mode 0700, and writes the body as UTF-8 using requested mode 0600. The returned ordered references contain only {name, path}, with path relative to artifactDirectory. These checks use the host's basename semantics; they do not add a platform-independent path grammar or reject dot/empty basenames in advance. Such names can still fail at write time. Repeated same-category/run/name writes overwrite the same path and can yield repeated references; there is no content deduplication, exclusive-create option or rollback transaction. Mode arguments apply to creation and do not force a chmod of preexisting paths (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/artifacts.ts:87-112).

The direct suite was fully read: it checks explicit-task registration, run/type filtering, 64-hex run directories and exact persisted contents. It does not cover malformed attachment names, overwrite collisions or injected I/O failures. Session/source contents are retained unredacted by this helper, matching the README's description of prompts/responses/source/tool-output artifacts.

A per-test callback persists attachments and appends a JSONL run record when an artifact directory is configured. A separate end-of-run pass derives observations from test metadata and prints the paired comparison report. An interrupted run suppresses that aggregate comparison without erasing already written per-test records.

It does not directly serialize the output, normalized transcript or test.meta().eval.avgScore into this local index (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:14-44).

Attachment persistence happens before creating the root and appending runs.jsonl. The root is requested recursively with mode 0700; appendFile uses UTF-8, flag'a' and mode 0600. There is no local index deduplication, file lock, whole-record transaction with attachments, or recovery rollback. I/O errors propagate from the awaited callback; attachments may exist even when the later index append fails. Other reporters may emit their own formats, but those external formats are not inferred here (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:42-50; ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:96-98).

collectHarnessObservations enumerates every module's allTests, requires a recognized harness run and a successfully parsed vitestEvalsHarnessIteration artifact, and copies evalSet/groupKey/harness/baseline/candidates/repetition. Pairing uses module.relativeModuleId and test.name, not fullName. avgScore and estimatedCostUsd are accepted only when typeof number and finite. totalTokens and totalMs are copied when not undefined; the summary later rejects non-finite metric pairs. If run.errors is nonempty, outcome is errored even when a judge score exists. Otherwise a finite judge score creates a scored observation regardless of the Vitest result state. Without a score, passed becomes unscored, failed becomes errored, and other test states pass through. A failed hard assertion with an existing finite score and no harness-run error is therefore still scored for this comparison, although Vitest may fail the test (ice:packages/evals/src/vitest-evals/reporter.ts:53-87).

onInit stores the Vitest logger. onTestRunEnd ignores its serialized-error argument; reason==='interrupted' prints the unavailable message and returns. Other end reasons summarize and format the collected observations, printing only nonempty output. Tests that never produced a recognized harness run or iteration artifact are not synthesized into observations; a missing counterpart can only be diagnosed where another observed run declares the comparison. The local inventory has no dedicated reporter unit suite, so these branches are source-read only.

Both runs ask the model to create a hello tool accepting a name, reload the session, then ask it to call the tool for Bob and respond with exactly the greeting. The source path is a fixed expected hello.ts even though the first prompt does not explicitly name that file. The judge fails when that source is unavailable. It extracts imports with a regex matching from/import followed by whitespace and a quoted specifier; this is not a TypeScript parser and does not inspect dynamic import(...) forms. It requires a canonical @zykairotis/ice-coding-agent import, rejects matched @mariozechner/* or @sinclair/typebox* imports, requires zero loader errors and a loaded 'hello' tool, and requires a normalized successful call named hello with arguments.name==='Bob' and result==='Hello, Bob!'. Final response must equal 'Hello, Bob!' exactly without trimming. All conditions must pass for score1; otherwise score0 with semicolon-joined rationale metadata (ice:packages/evals/src/extensions.eval.ts:53-98).

describeEval receives that judge and judgeThreshold:null, expressing observational scoring rather than a score threshold gate. The test records hello.ts as a text/typescript UTF-8 source artifact when source exists, requiring a string runId first. It then hard-asserts that Guidelines/documentation markers match whether the harness name is 'default-system-prompt'. The README directs comparative suites to use judges for correctness and hard assertions only for setup/infrastructure invariants; it states that expect.soft still fails a test. That external framework behavior is not independently executed here. Four local unit suites test helper contracts, while the two *.eval.ts files are model-backed scenarios whose outcomes remain unverified.

normalizePath can trim input, normalize selected Unicode spaces and strip a leading '@' when requested; it expands '~' and '~/' (also '~\\' on Windows), decodes file URLs and leaves ordinary relative paths relative. resolvePath supplies a base; canonicalPath tries realpath and falls back to the resolved path. Do not equate these string and filesystem operations or claim all callers perform every optional normalization.

The explicit markPathIgnoredByCloudSync(path) utility sets Darwin attributes com.dropbox.ignored and com.apple.fileprovider.ignore#P with xattr -w <attr> 1 <path>, or Linux user.com.dropbox.ignored with setfattr -n <attr> -v 1 <path>. paragraphs: `FileSettingsStorage` resolves cwd and agentDir and uses `<agentDir>/settings.json` and `<cwd>/.ice/settings.json`. `withLock(scope,fn)` checks existence. For an existing file it acquires a proper-lockfile lock with `realpath:false`, reads UTF-8, and calls fn with current text; for a missing file it calls fn(undefined) without creating or locking anything first. Undefined callback output means no write. If a string is returned it creates the directory when necessary, obtains a lock if none is held, writes directly, and releases in finally. A first-file write therefore computes the callback before acquiring its write lock; the audit does not claim that initial creation is a fully serialized read-modify-write. Lock acquisition retries ELOCKED at most 10 times with 20 ms synchronous waits; other/final failures propagate.

Loading an untrusted project returns an empty object before touching project storage. Missing or empty text means an empty object. Otherwise JSON.parse and migration require a non-null non-array object; comments are not accepted by this TS settings reader. Each scope is loaded independently: tryLoad returns an empty object plus the error on first-load failure. Error diagnostics retain the failing scope. `getLoadErrors` returns a frozen non-consuming list of active load errors; `drainErrors` consumes the accumulated diagnostic queue. Save updates effective memory and notifies listeners, but does not schedule a write for a scope with an unresolved initial/load error.

records.full_text:
Theme discovery reads JSON files from the ordered resource paths and isolates each file's load failure as a warning. A separate name-deduplication pass keeps the first theme and reports the source path of later collisions before optional caller overrides and source enrichment.

With includeDefaults true the low-level helper visits agentDir/themes then cwd/.ice/themes; the resource loader normally supplies already-resolved paths with includeDefaults false. Explicit directories are scanned nonrecursively in inNodeReaddirOrder. Regular .json files and symlinks resolving to regular files are accepted; broken symlinks are skipped. Missing explicit paths warn, non-JSON/non-file paths warn, and directory/stat/parser exceptions become diagnostics while other themes continue loading. Additional missing theme paths also receive the resource-loader's explicit-path error diagnostic.

Each file is delegated to loadThemeFromPath, whose JSON/color/variable validation belongs to TUI. The deduper selects by theme.name; when two different source paths share a name, it records winnerPath/loserPath. Repeating the same source path is ignored. Missing source paths use the builtin marker when forming collision details, and undefined names follow the same Map-key rule rather than gaining generated identities. themesOverride receives the deduplicated list and accumulated diagnostics, after which package/extension SourceInfo is attached from sourcePath.

noThemes removes automatic sources but explicitly supplied additional paths can still be loaded through the resource orchestration contract. Merely collecting extension themePaths does not prove a host can parse, list or select those themes.
